back: Trade between countries without government restrictions such as tariffs, quotas, subsidies or embargoes.
Countries that remove tariffs and quotas on trade among themselves but keep their own barriers against non-members.

front: On what theory is the case for free trade based?
back: Specialisation according to comparative advantage, which raises world output.

front: Give four advantages of free trade.
back: Lower prices and more choice; higher world output; larger markets and economies of scale; competition and efficiency; cheaper inputs; technology transfer.

front: Give four disadvantages of free trade.
back: Harm to infant industries; job losses; dumping; dependence on few exports and on imports; loss of tariff revenue; current account problems.

front: What happens to government revenue when tariffs are removed?
back: Customs duty revenue falls, so other taxes must rise or spending must fall.

front: When was the World Trade Organization set up?
back: In 1995; it provides a forum for negotiating lower trade barriers and settling trade disputes.
High-cost local producers and their workers, and governments that relied on tariff revenue.
